one_sentence: Fiat currency is a thermodynamic fraud because it violates the conservation principle by injecting phantom money without corresponding real work, leading to systemic degradation.
executive_summary: This document establishes a structural isomorphism between the First Law of Thermodynamics (energy conservation) and sound monetary policy (gold standard), arguing that fiat currency, created by institutional decree without real backing, constitutes a conservation violation analogous to injecting phantom energy into a closed system. The key evidence includes historical fiat currency failures (Roman denarius, Continental Dollar, Assignat, Reichsmark, Zimbabwe dollar) and post-1971 economic data showing inflation, inequality, and debt accumulation. The conclusion is that fiat systems inevitably degrade due to this structural violation, and the mapping reveals a theological dimension where such monetary fraud violates divine moral order.
short_summary: This document is an isomorphism record mapping the First Law of Thermodynamics to monetary policy. The core structural claim is that fiat currency creation without real backing is a conservation violation analogous to injecting phantom energy into a physical system. Key evidence includes historical fiat currency failures and post-1971 economic data showing inflation and inequality. This matters because it reframes monetary policy as a thermodynamic and moral issue, predicting inevitable degradation of fiat systems.
